skill: Identify possible or impossible slope fields from dependence on x, y, or both, by comparing slope variation along vertical and horizontal lines.
learner_operation: Determine the variables on which the RHS depends; inspect constancy or variation of segment slopes along fixed-x and fixed-y lines; select the unique field satisfying (or violating) the specified dependence. Explicit-equation questions must also depict that equation rather than merely an arbitrary two-variable field.
reasoning_steps: Compare slopes along horizontal and vertical lines, avoiding exceptional zero-slope lines as sole witnesses.
Apply could/cannot polarity and select the unique image.
Explain the directional variation with a representative horizontal/vertical line.
response_contract: Practice questions: one radio field with five separate image choices. Canonical e-8507 has four labeled panels I–IV in a composite image, with no captured structured answer field; its solution supplies the correct field. No free entry or ODE solving.
difficulty: Moderate: explicit xy, y-x^2, exp(xy) and canonical x+y. Hard: generic both-dependent f and cannot with a one-variable outlier. Missing-difficulty duplicate cannot source is incomplete.
invariants: Comparable slope-field image choices and one correct response; five choices in practice, four in the canonical composite
Could vs cannot follows source difficulty families
No integration, solution curves, or multi-select
All panels must use the same visual conventions
permitted_variations: Nonzero coefficients and signs in the observed simple RHS families
Which compatible image occupies the answer role
For cannot, either missing x or missing y dependence as independently witnessed in source
One-variable distractor profiles and signs without requiring extra prerequisites

fixed_features.feature: Both-dependent RHS in moderate could questions
fixed_features.justification: This KP's sources and lesson explicitly contrast both-dependence with the prerequisite autonomous/nonautonomous one-variable cases. Selecting the only two-variable field is the intended operation, not by itself a shortcut.
Single radio response requires uniqueness, but its position, sign, or incidental drawing style need not be fixed.

answer_roles: Correct index may vary across all five images
Hard impossible image may be x-only or y-only
Moderate compatible image's shape and sign should follow the explicit RHS
Annotations may identify the selected image only in the worked solution, never in answer choices
